record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Which square-free words u can be shuffled to obtain a square-free word u ▷β u?

evidence.quote: Which square-free words u can be shuffled to obtain a square-free word u β u? 

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is called a square if $w = xx$ for some nonempty $x \in \Sigma^*$, and $w$ is square-free if no factor (contiguous subword) of $w$ is a square.

Given two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$, the shuffle set $u \shuffle v$ is the set of all words obtained by interleaving $u$ and $v$ while preserving the relative order of the letters within each: formally, $w \in u \shuffle v$ iff $w = u_1 v_1 u_2 v_2 \cdots u_k v_k$ for some factorizations $u = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$ and $v = v_1 v_2 \cdots v_k$ (where the $u_i, v_i$ may be empty).

Characterize the square-free words $u \in \Sigma^*$ for which there exists at least one square-free word in $u \shuffle u$ (i.e., $u$ can be shuffled with itself to produce a square-free word).
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known. Currie (2013/2015, "Square-Free Shuffles of Words") showed that for every n ≥ 3 there exists a square-free ternary word u of length n such that u⧢u contains a square-free word, and that there are infinite square-free ternary words u such that u⧢u contains an infinite square-free word. Harju and others studied infinite self-shuffling square-free words. However, a complete characterization of which square-free words u admit a square-free shuffle u⧢u does not appear to have been given, so the underlying classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Square-Free Shuffles of Words
status_evidence.snippet: For each n ≥ 3 there is a square-free ternary word of length n such that u⧢u contains a square-free word; an infinite analogue is also given.
status_evidence.claim: Existence (not full characterization) of square-free words admitting square-free self-shuffles is established.

status_evidence.title: On Shuffling of Infinite Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies infinite square-free words that can be shuffled with themselves to give a square-free word.
status_evidence.claim: Further results on infinite-word version of the question, but not a complete characterization.

status_evidence.title: Infinite square-free self-shuffling words
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs infinite square-free words that are self-shuffling.
